Unbelievable Fish Batter
4.7
(565)
496 Reviews
72 Photos
Jump to Recipe
This fish batter recipe makes the lightest, crispiest batter imaginable! I got this recipe on an open-line, talk-radio show in the early 1950s and it has been a family favorite ever since. It makes enough to coat approximately 2 pounds of fish.

Submitted by MargeBC  Updated on January 21, 2026
 Tested by Isabelle Easter

Fried fish served on fries, with tartar sauce and ketchup in a basket

72

Prep Time:
10 mins
Total Time:
10 mins
Servings:
6
Yield:
2 1/4 cups
Jump to Nutrition Facts
This fish batter recipe ensures flavorful and crispy fried fish that’s surprisingly simple to make at home. The batter is seasoned with salt and you can add additional spices like paprika or seafood seasoning for an additional boost of flavor, if desired. You can use this batter to fry fish for pub-style fish and chips or fish tacos. 

Fish Batter Ingredients
You’ll find a detailed ingredient list and step-by-step instructions in the recipe below, but let’s go over the basics:

Flour: This simple fish batter recipe starts with all-purpose flour. 
Milk: The proteins in milk help the batter adhere to the fish and promote browning. 
Water: Use very cold water for the crispiest results. 
Baking powder: Baking powder ensures a light and crispy exterior. 
Salt: A teaspoon of salt enhances the overall flavor of the fish batter.
What Is the Best Fish for Frying?
The best fish for frying is white, mild, lean, and has a sturdy texture that stands up well to the hot oil. Great choices include cod, haddock, tilapia, and flounder. This batter is also great for shrimp.

How to Use Fish Batter
Here’s how to use this easy fish batter:

Heat oil in a deep fryer to 365 degrees F (185 degrees C). 
Pat fish dry before coating it in batter to ensure it sticks. 
Dip fish fillets into the batter to coat. 
Carefully lower fillets, one at a time, into the hot oil. Fry several fillets at a time, turning once, until cooked through and golden brown, about 2 minutes per side. 
Drain on paper towels.
Allrecipes Community Tips and Praise
“When you want that authentic puffy fish and chips shop result, this does not disappoint,” according to ThatchWright. “Best batter recipe I have tried for fish.”

Editorial contributions by Corey Williams

Keep Screen Awake
Ingredients

1/2x

1x

2x

Original recipe (1X) yields 6 servings

1 cup all-purpose flour

1/2 cup milk

1/2 cup water

2 tablespoons baking powder

1 teaspoon salt

Directions
Gather ingredients.

Prep ingredients for fish batter, including flour, milk, water, salt, and baking powder
Photographer: Morgan Hunt Glaze / Food Styling: Anna Kelley / Prop Styling: Julia Bayless 
Whisk flour, milk, water, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl until smooth.

A bowl of batter with a whisk being held and stirred
Photographer: Morgan Hunt Glaze / Food Styling: Anna Kelley / Prop Styling: Julia Bayless 
To Use:
Heat vegetable or canola oil in a deep fryer to 365 degrees F (185 degrees C).

A pot of oil with a thermometer on a stove
Photographer: Morgan Hunt Glaze / Food Styling: Anna Kelley / Prop Styling: Julia Bayless 
Pat fish fillets dry with paper towels to help ensure batter sticks; dip fish fillets into the batter to coat.

Pieces of fish immersed in batter inside a glass bowl
Photographer: Morgan Hunt Glaze / Food Styling: Anna Kelley / Prop Styling: Julia Bayless 
Carefully lower fillets, one at a time, into hot oil. Fry several fillets at a time without overcrowding the pan, turning once, until cooked through and golden brown, about 2 minutes per side.

A hand holding battered fish over a pot of hot oil, with a thermometer in the oil measuring the temperature
Photographer: Morgan Hunt Glaze / Food Styling: Anna Kelley / Prop Styling: Julia Bayless 
Drain fried fish fillets on a wire rack over a paper-towel lined pan.

Two battered fish fillets on a cooling rack
Photographer: Morgan Hunt Glaze / Food Styling: Anna Kelley / Prop Styling: Julia Bayless 
Serve hot and enjoy.

Fried fish served on fries, with tartar sauce and ketchup in a basket
Photographer: Morgan Hunt Glaze / Food Styling: Anna Kelley / Prop Styling: Julia Bayless 
From the Editor
This recipe was tested in our test kitchen and the amount of baking powder was reduced to 2 tablespoons for best results. The original recipe called for 1/4 cup baking powder.
